## Solution: Windows

```r
library(future)
library(furrr)
starts <- c(-5, 0, 5, 10)

plan(multisession, workers = 2)
chains <- future_map(
  starts,
  \(s) mh_chain(n = 30000, start = s),
  .options = furrr_options(seed = 323)
)
sapply(chains, \(x) mean(tail(x, 10000)))
plan(sequential)
```

`multisession` launches separate R sessions and works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Solution: macOS / Linux (when forking is supported)

<!-- chains <- future_map( -->
                             <!--   starting_values, -->
                             <!--   function(starting_value) { -->
                                 <!--     mh_chain(n = 30000, start = starting_value) -->
                                 <!--   }, -->
                             <!--   .options = furrr_options(seed = 323) -->
                             <!-- ) -->
  
  ```r
library(future)
library(furrr)
starts <- c(-5, 0, 5, 10)

plan(multicore, workers = 2)
chains <- future_map(
  starts,
  \(s) mh_chain(n = 30000, start = s),
  .options = furrr_options(seed = 323)
)
sapply(chains, \(x) mean(tail(x, 10000)))
plan(sequential)
```

`multicore` uses process forking; check `parallelly::supportsMulticore()` first. In RStudio or other environments where forking is unsupported, use `multisession` instead.

**Key point:** Each chain is sequential; the **four chains** are independent jobs.
